source_title: Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme - GovtSchemes.in
source_excerpt:
The scheme offers financial assistance of up to ₹10 crore for eligible commercial layer and pullet farming projects.
It supports the establishment of modern, fully automated poultry farms with over 25,000 birds.
Aims to increase Odisha’s egg production and reduce the gap between local egg demand and supply.
Fisheries and Animal Resources Development (FARD) Department Helpline Number: 0674-2536985 0674-2322960
The Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme, known in Odia as "Byabasayika Andadia Kukudapalana Yojana", is a newly introduced initiative of the Fisheries and Animal Resources Development (FARD) Department , Government of Odisha. The scheme was formally launched on 9 October 2026 on the occasion of World Egg Day by Fisheries and Animal Resources Development Minister Shri Gokulananda Mallik at the Veterinary Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.
The primary purpose of this scheme is to strengthen Odisha's egg production capacity and reduce the gap between local demand and supply. At present, the state's daily egg production stands at approximately 1.12 crore eggs, while the annual per capita availability remains around 87 eggs against the national average of 106 eggs. Recognising this shortfall, the state government has set an ambitious target of achieving an annual production of 1,000 crore eggs by the year 2036.
The Commercial Layer Farming Scheme has been designed as a key instrument to realise this long-term vision by encouraging the establishment of large-scale, modern and fully automated commercial layer and pullet farms across the state.
Under the scheme, the department will give incentives for setting up modern, fully automated commercial layer and pullet farms with a capacity of more than 25,000 birds. An eligible unit can receive government financial assistance of up to ₹10 crore. The scheme reportedly provides a portion of the subsidy in advance through a “Mirror Account” mechanism to help reduce entrepreneurs’ interest burden on bank loans. Until now, large layer farms could get only up to ₹1 crore under the Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana (MKUY) , so the new scheme raises the support ceiling for big automated units tenfold.
The Commercial Layer Farming Scheme works on a credit-linked, project-based model: an entrepreneur plans a large automated farm, arranges a bank loan, and the government shares part of the capital cost. Although the scheme has been formally announced, the detailed operational guidelines have not yet been published by the Fisheries and Animal Resources Development Department.
Similar to Odisha’s Commercial Layer Farming Scheme, the Central Government also runs the National Livestock Mission (NLM) to support the establishment of rural poultry breeding units and promote entrepreneurship in the poultry sector through financial assistance. You can explore the complete details of this scheme here.
The Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme primarily provides capital support to entrepreneurs establishing large-scale, automated layer and pullet farms in Odisha. The following benefits are covered under the scheme:
Financial Assistance: Up to ₹10 crore of government assistance per eligible project (official department poster).
Higher Support Cap: Large automated units can now get up to ₹10 crore, against the earlier ₹1 crore limit under MKUY.
Advance Subsidy: Media reports state that the subsidy will reach entrepreneurs in advance through a Mirror Account linked to the bank loan, which lowers the interest burden.
Support for Modern Technology: The scheme promotes fully automated feeding, watering, egg collection, and climate-controlled housing systems.
Business Opportunity: It helps new entrepreneurs enter a sector where local demand already exceeds local supply.
Applicants must meet the following eligibility conditions to apply for the Commercial Layer Farming Scheme.
The applicant must establish a modern, fully automated commercial layer farm or pullet farm.
The farm must have a capacity of more than 25,000 birds.
The applicant category, age limit, land requirements, bank loan conditions, and other eligibility criteria have not yet been officially published by the concerned authority.
The FARD Department has not published any official document list for this scheme yet. We will update this section once the operational guideline names the required documents. Applicants should not rely on unofficial checklists shared on social media.
The Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme is currently at the announcement stage. The Fisheries and Animal Resources Development Department has not yet released the detailed operational guidelines. Therefore, official information regarding the application process is not yet available. Once the department issues the complete guidelines, the verified application details will be updated in this article.
Visit the FARD Department website regularly and check the scheme and notice sections.
Contact the office of the Chief District Veterinary Officer (CDVO) in your district for the latest information on the scheme.
Discuss project financing with your bank in advance, because the announced Mirror Account subsidy is linked to bank loans.

1. What is the Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme?
It is a new Odisha government scheme that gives up to ₹10 crore of assistance for setting up modern, automated commercial layer and pullet farms with a capacity of more than 25,000 birds.
The scheme is called "Byabasayika Andadia Kukudapalana Yojana" in Odia.
3. How much assistance can an entrepreneur get?
An eligible project can get government assistance of up to ₹10 crore. The department has not yet notified the subsidy percentage.
4. Can a small poultry farmer with 2,000 birds apply?
No. The scheme targets farms above 25,000 birds. Semi-commercial farmers with 1,000 to 4,000 birds can look at the separate state support of up to ₹19.74 lakh.
5. How can I apply for the Odisha Commercial Layer Farming Scheme?
Applications have not started yet. The department has not announced an online portal or offline process.
6. What is the egg production target under the scheme?
Odisha aims to produce 1,000 crore eggs a year by 2036.
